citations.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 2012; entry credited to 胡偉
citations.field: PDF p. 708, printed p. 695; 白部 entry; scan inspected
citations.text: The entry says the graph’s construction is disputed and attributes the thumb pictograph account to Guo Moruo. It describes a sequence from oracle-bone to bronze, small-seal, and regular script forms. This verifies what the book reports; it does not establish the thumb as the graph’s original referent.

citations.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 2012; entry credited to 胡偉
citations.field: PDF p. 708, printed p. 695; 白部 entry; scan inspected
citations.text: The entry presents a word-history proposal: the thumb account connects 白 with 伯 through the thumb’s supposed leading position, then treats use for the color word as borrowing. It says the color sense extends to purity; daylight motivates “bright,” which extends to clear or understood, then to state or argue a case, and to tell or report. It cites literary examples but supplies no dates for this proposed sequence.

consulted_citations.field: PDF p. 301, printed p. 289; 白(自) entry; scan inspected
consulted_citations.text: This is a separate headword 白(自), read zì, describing an alternate nose-pictograph form associated with 自. The entry says the forms were used for the same word in early writing and later became differentiated. It is not the 白 bái headword on printed page 695 and should not be merged with that entry.
